alt: A table of comparison counts for finding the middle value of a list, for growing list sizes. One column uses the first element as the pivot and one uses a random pivot. On sorted input the first-element column grows about four times each time the size doubles, while the random column roughly doubles.

steps.caption: For n = 100, finding the middle value compares 3825 times with the first-element pivot and 374 times with a random pivot.
n doubles to 200. The first-element pivot now compares 15150 times, 4.0 times the previous row. The random pivot compares 464 times, 1.2 times the previous row.
n doubles to 400. The first-element pivot now compares 60300 times, 4.0 times the previous row. The random pivot compares 787 times, 1.7 times the previous row.
n doubles to 800. The first-element pivot now compares 240600 times, 4.0 times the previous row. The random pivot compares 2783 times, 3.5 times the previous row.
n doubles to 1600. The first-element pivot now compares 961200 times, 4.0 times the previous row. The random pivot compares 5646 times, 2.0 times the previous row.
